clean-body.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Create ONE usable transparent registered game-animation layer, not a concept sheet. The reference is the edit target. Keep the same full 1210 by 1300 portrait canvas, scale, and positions; do not recenter, crop, zoom, or expand the character. Preserve the purple reaper's head, hood, green eyes, skull face, left-side relaxed hand and sleeve, body robe, belt, gold skull clasp, cape, legs and boots exactly in their original placement and original painted cartoon game style. Remove completely the scythe weapon, the fist gripping it on the VIEWER RIGHT, and the entire viewer-right hanging weapon-arm sleeve from shoulder to wrist. Reconstruct the small hidden right edge of the torso robe behind that removed arm so the body is closed, clean and continuous. The shoulder mantle can remain on the torso; it must end naturally with no detached arm stump, no second hand, no fist silhouette, no wooden pole residue and no scythe blade anywhere. Areas that the removed weapon/arm occupied outside the torso must be genuinely transparent. This is the clean stationary BODY BASE behind separately animated arm pieces. It should show an armless right side under the shoulder cloak, not a new lowered right arm. Keep all other original art, palette and line weights. Real alpha transparency, no ground shadow, background, checkerboard, text, guide marks or extra objects. Return only this one clean body-base layer in the same frame as the reference.

hand-scythe.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Create ONE usable transparent registered game-animation layer, not a sheet or diagram. Use the reference as the edit target. Keep the same full 1210 by 1300 portrait canvas, exact object scale and original placement; do not zoom, center the extracted object, rotate or crop. Keep ONLY the complete large curved metal scythe blade, its complete wooden shaft and pointed lower end, and the bony gripping fist at upper-chest height on the VIEWER RIGHT, exactly as they appear in the reference. The fingers correctly wrap in front of the shaft; the pole remains in the fist without any change to the grip. Add a short anatomically plausible wrist-bone stump emerging down-left from the base of that same fist, just enough to disappear into a separate sleeve cuff; the wrist-root end should be rounded, complete and about 40 source pixels long, not chopped exactly at the visible wrist line. Do not add another hand. Remove every purple garment, sleeve, cape, shoulder, body, head, belt, feet and every other part of the character completely to transparency. No purple cloth stuck to the hand, no shoulder, no full arm, no ghost outlines of the removed body. The output is a single coupled HAND-AND-SCYTHE layer whose grip cannot slip when the layer rotates at the wrist. Preserve the exact style, scythe silhouette, blade proportions, shading, thick outlines and original wooden shaft. Keep the blade and spike fully in frame. True transparent background, no text, no labels, no shadow, no checkerboard.
